brief:
Famine in Gaza has become a stark test of a system where politics, economics, and ethics compete at the expense of basic sustenance, Shehab Wire reported. As international aid retreats under funding pressure and food programs affecting hundreds of people halt, the humanitarian crisis deepens across the territory.

The situation reflects a dual crisis: an external blockade restricting supplies and internal monopolistic practices that compound shortages for civilians already facing severe deprivation.

title: Hunger in Gaza stems from external blockade and internal monopoly
